record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: What is the finite-sample performance of the k-nearest-neighbor decision rule when the training set is finite rather than infinite?

evidence.quote: How fast does the error rate Pe[k-NN] approach the Bayes error Pe as n approaches infinity, and what is the finite-sample performance of the k-NN-rule

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,Y)$ be a random pair taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d \times \{1,2,\dots,M\}$ with joint distribution $\mathbb{P}$, and let the regression/posterior functions be $\eta_j(x) = \mathbb{P}(Y=j \mid X=x)$ for $j=1,\dots,M$. The Bayes classifier is $g^*(x) = \arg\max_{j} \eta_j(x)$, with Bayes error $P_e^* = \mathbb{P}(g^*(X) \neq Y)$.

Given an i.i.d. training sample $D_n = \{(X_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ from $\mathbb{P}$, and a positive integer $k \le n$, the $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) decision rule $g_{n,k}$ classifies a query point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ by majority vote among the labels $Y_{(1)}(x),\dots,Y_{(k)}(x)$ of the $k$ training points whose features $X_{(i)}(x)$ are nearest to $x$ in Euclidean distance (ties broken by a fixed rule). Its conditional error probability is
$$P_e[k\text{-NN}](n) = \mathbb{P}\big(g_{n,k}(X) \neq Y \mid D_n\big),$$
and its expected error is $\mathbb{E}\,P_e[k\text{-NN}](n)$.

Provide a quantitative characterization of the finite-sample performance of the $k$-NN rule. Specifically, for general (or suitably specified) distributions $\mathbb{P}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d \times \{1,\dots,M\}$ and finite $n$, determine sharp non-asymptotic upper and lower bounds on
$$\mathbb{E}\,P_e[k\text{-NN}](n) - P_e^*$$
as a function of $n$, $k$, the dimension $d$, and meaningful structural parameters of $\mathbb{P}$ (such as smoothness or margin conditions on $\eta_j$), and identify the choice of $k = k(n)$ that minimizes this finite-sample excess risk.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on finite-sample bounds for k-NN classification: non-asymptotic high-probability upper bounds in general metric spaces (Chaudhuri–Dasgupta), minimax-optimal rates of order n^{-4/(d+4)} under smoothness and margin (Tsybakov) conditions, and asymptotic expansions of k-NN risk are known. However, sharp distribution-free finite-sample characterizations and matching upper/lower bounds in full generality remain incomplete, so the broad question is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Rates of convergence for nearest neighbor classification (Chaudhuri–Dasgupta)
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-sample, distribution-dependent upper bounds on k-NN misclassification in general metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Non-asymptotic finite-sample bounds for k-NN have been established in general metric spaces.

status_evidence.title: Rate of Convergence of k-Nearest-Neighbor Classification Rule (JMLR)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes convergence rates of k-NN classification under smoothness/margin conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence rates of k-NN to the Bayes error are characterized under regularity assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic expansions of the k-nearest neighbor risk
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order asymptotic expansions of the k-NN risk are derived.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic (but not fully finite-sample sharp) expansions of k-NN risk are available.
